item.title: Google Stitch to WordPress: How to Turn a Stitch Design into an Editable WordPress Site
item.description: Google Stitch designs good-looking screens and exports them as HTML with Tailwind CSS. Here is how to put those screens on WordPress as real, editable pages—without rebuilding them in a page builder.

item.title: Lovable, Bolt or v0 Site to WordPress? An Honest Guide to What Works Today
item.description: Lovable, Bolt and v0 build React apps, and the page only exists after their build runs. Here are your real options for getting one onto WordPress—including when an HTML importer like Kerf can’t help yet.

item.title: Your AI-Made Website’s Contact Form Doesn’t Send? How to Make It Work on WordPress
item.description: The contact form in an AI-generated HTML site looks finished but posts nowhere. Here is why, the usual fixes, and how Kerf makes the same form email you and save every message in WordPress—keeping its design.

item.title: Changed the Design After Launch? How to Update an AI-Made WordPress Site Without Losing Your Edits
item.description: You imported an AI-made design, then edited text and photos in WordPress. Now the design has changed. Here is how to apply the new version section by section—without overwriting what you already edited.

item.title: How to Turn an AI-Generated HTML Website into a WordPress Site in One Click (Without Elementor or Rebuilding)
item.description: You asked Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini to design a website and got a gorgeous HTML/CSS/JS folder. Here is how to put that same design on WordPress in one click, its HTML and CSS kept as written, with full block editing.

item.title: ChatGPT, Claude & Gemini Write Great Websites — Here Is the Exact Prompt Brief to Make Them WordPress-Ready
item.description: Copy our battle-tested prompt template for Claude Artifacts, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google Stitch so the HTML ZIP you generate imports into WordPress with working menus, forms, and live blog templates.

item.title: Why Page Builders Ruin Custom HTML Designs (And How Zero-Wrapper Block Conversion Fixes It)
item.description: A technical look at why importing custom HTML into widget builders or standard WordPress blocks breaks child combinators, CSS Grid, and SVG icons—and how Kerf preserves the exact DOM.

item.title: The 2026 Agency Playbook: Ship Custom WordPress Client Sites in an Afternoon with AI and Kerf
item.description: How freelancers and web agencies combine AI design generation with Kerf’s multi-page importer, section-by-section updates, Site Details, and Client Mode to deliver higher-margin WordPress projects.

item.title: Static HTML Hosting vs. WordPress for AI Websites: Why Clients Still Need a Real CMS
item.description: Hosting an AI-generated HTML file on a static host takes two minutes—until the client asks to publish blog posts, edit text without code, manage SEO metadata, or view form leads. Here is how to get both.

item.title: Bring Your Own Gemini Key: How to Build and Edit Custom WordPress Pages with Kerf AI (With Zero Monthly AI Markup)
item.description: Many WordPress AI plugins sell AI as a monthly credit subscription. Kerf AI connects directly to your own Google Gemini API key to build full sites, turn Word docs into styled pages, and edit sections in place.
